problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: Rosser''s 1936 improvement: can this formalization be extended to use only plain consistency (not ω-consistency) by replacing G with the Rosser sentence R defined via a proof-length comparison?.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Rosser 1936 formalized. 3 axioms (vs Gödel 5), 0 sorries, 11 theorems. Equi-decidability (⊢R ↔ ⊢¬R) is the key. omega_consistency_G eliminated. Gallery entry created.
builtItems: R_not_provable: R is not provable under plain consistency
R_not_disprovable: ¬R is not provable under plain consistency (replaces omega_consistency_G)
rosser_first_incompleteness: Every consistent system satisfying Rosser axioms is incomplete
R_undecidable: R is neither provable nor disprovable
godel_vs_rosser_comparison: Explicit theorem documenting the structural improvement
insights: Rosser sentence R satisfies equi-decidability: (⊢ R) ↔ (⊢ ¬R), the structural heart of the improvement
Plain consistency suffices for full undecidability of R — omega_consistency_G axiom is completely eliminated
Proof is symmetric: provability and disprovability both lead to contradiction with consistency via same argument
Only 3 axioms needed vs. 5 for Gödel: Provable + R_prov_gives_formal_disproof + R_disproof_gives_formal_prov
Rosser sentence R = ⟨43⟩ encodes: for every proof of R (code p), there exists disproof with code ≤ p
nextSteps: Consider formalization of Gödel Second Incompleteness: Con(F) is not provable in F (would need more axioms but could build on this structure)
The equi-decidability biconditional has broader implications — could explore Rosser-type sentences in more abstract settings
